free_tier.stated: Quoted: 'kontener LXC zarządzany przez Incus', 'do 2 GB RAM', 'do 10 GB limitu dysku (quota)', 'prawa root w VPS', 'dystrybucja Linuksa wybrana przez Ciebie'. Each container gets 'stały publiczny adres IPv6, nazwę hosta i rekord PTR', and incoming IPv4 arrives through forwarded ports on the host address. A shell account with 41 GB of quota plus 5 GB NextCloud and 5 GB Immich comes with it, and the quotas sum.

per_object_cap.stated: quoted: 'możliwość podmontowania zasobów konta shell w kontenerze' with the note that the shell quota and the VPS quota 'może być efektywnie zsumowana'. The VPS page states no per-account server count.

retention.stated: Quoted: 'Nie można posiadać VPS, o którym tu mowa, bez konta shell. Utrata konta shell, np. z powodu nieaktywności, jest równoznaczna z utratą VPS.' The terms also reserve the administrator's right to delete an account at any time without warning. No idle timeout is quantified for the VPS itself.

egress.terms: quoted for the shell host: '1 Gbps bez limitu danych w Niemczech' (1 Gbit/s, no data limit, in Germany). No separate allowance is stated for the container.

interface_detail: root in an Incus-managed LXC container, reachable over a static public IPv6 with a PTR record; IPv4 inbound through agreed port forwards from the host address; HTTP/HTTPS reverse proxy from host to container; SSH to the shell account with optional TOTP 2FA
tooling: any SSH client; Incus on the vendor side
chaining: The only free row that gives root and a public IPv6 with reverse DNS on a 1 Gbit/s unmetered link, which is what a WireGuard node or an IPv6-reachable monitor actually needs.

limits.value: 2 GB RAM and 10 GB disk per container; 41 GB plus 10 GB of side services on the shell account
a shell account is a precondition, and the administrator decides whether a VPS is created at all
losing the shell account, including through inactivity, loses the VPS

binding_note: Two human gates stand in front of the container: the shell account is manually approved, and the terms state that the administrator alone decides whether a VPS is created, and only for users 'z dłuższym stażem'.

identity_cost.detail: a one-off irreversible payment of PLN 0.01 as an identity check: the signup form carries 'Akceptuję to, że założenie konta wymaga bezzwrotnej wpłaty 0,01 PLN jako elementu weryfikacji tożsamości'. The form also asks first and last name, email, a login, and an IRC nick on #wtw, and the terms require presence on that channel. No card hold beyond the PLN 0.01, no phone, no document.

reliability_note: No reliability event observed. The project states it is hobbyist and non-commercial and that it 'nie zapewniają jakości usług porównywalnych z ofertami komercyjnymi'.
confidence_note: Shape, the root statement, the IPv6 arrangement, the PLN 0.01 gate and the two-stage approval are quoted from the project's own pages read. Whether a VPS is granted in practice, and how long it takes, is not established: the terms make it discretionary and cannot register.

notes: The best shape and the most conditional: a root LXC container with up to 2 GB of RAM, 10 GB of disk, a static public IPv6 with a PTR record, agreed IPv4 port forwards, and a 1 Gbit/s unmetered German uplink, for a one-off PLN 0.01 identity payment. What it costs is patience and a human: the shell account is manually approved, the container is granted only to users with standing, presence on an IRC channel is a stated condition, and the administrator may delete the account at any time without warning. The PLN 0.01 is a real payment, so the identity kind is card rather than email, but it is not a hold and not a subscription. Cannot register, so 'the administrator grants it' is the one link in the chain not observed. Recorded as reported-by-the-project, not as delivered.

extras.term: indefinite while the shell account is active
extras.price_arithmetic: PLN 0.01 once, for identity verification; the container itself is PLN 0.00 with no recurring charge and no published rate to multiply

network_out.ports: agreed ports forwarded from the host IPv4, plus a full public IPv6 per container

session_cap.note: no idle kill published for the container; the shell account carries an inactivity rule that is not quantified on the pages read
